benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Eased to about $114.88 on 27 Oct (Trading Economics), down roughly 0.8% on the day but still up about 3% w/w, after Monday's unconfirmed Houthi claims of fresh strikes on the East-West pipeline and Riyadh's airport and a fire near the Ras Tanura export terminal early Tuesday kept a geopolitical premium in the market even as Brent and WTI fell on profit-taking Monday after the prior week's rally. Week-ago is this site's 20 Oct reading, exactly 7 days earlier.

note: Brent and WTI slipped on 26 October on profit-taking after the prior week's rally, even as the Houthis claimed fresh, unconfirmed strikes on the East-West pipeline and Riyadh's airport; a fire then broke out near Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura export terminal early on 27 October (Bloomberg), with the extent of the damage unclear. TTF and JKM both extended their rallies to fresh 2026 highs on tight winter gas supply. Henry Hub continued easing, staying largely insulated from the Gulf turmoil.
